blindSummary:
Nothing criminalises being trans in this country, but violence against LGBT people is severe and documented: an LGBT community observatory recorded 147 cases of day-to-day violence and at least 29 murders of LGBTQIA+ people in 2022, with 35 victims saying they intended to flee the country. The state has explicitly excluded trans women from femicide-law protection on the grounds that they are not "biological women." There is no legal gender recognition and no SOGI hate-crime statute (a 2022 law actually increased penalties for "aggravated" LGBT visibility before being struck down).

The legislature has repeatedly advanced anti-LGBT initiatives (a 2022 "life and family protection" law, later shelved after protests). The community is organised (national LGBT organisations and trans collectives) but under pressure. The country's best-known tourist destinations are accustomed to foreigners but are not insulated from the general level of violence.
blindOutOfScope: General gang violence affects all travellers; the femicide-law exclusion is resident-facing but signals the institutional stance.

Encyclopedia article on transfemicide (the killing of trans women motivated by transphobic and misogynistic hatred), with coverage spanning this country's continent and beyond; relevant background for this country's context of violence against trans women.

Philanthropic-foundation report (May 2024): a regional human-rights court's 2017 advisory opinion on gender identity advanced legal gender recognition in four countries of this region, including this one, but a growing, vociferous opposition movement seeking to define gender in strictly binary terms is fomenting backlash in all four.
LGBT news outlet abroad (Dec 2017): a transgender rights bill was introduced in this country's legislature - the first legislative attempt at gender-identity protections in the country.

International human-rights organisation (Jan 2022): reports that an anti-trans bill threatens rights - documents legislative attacks on trans people, including bills that would erase gender identity protections and restrict legal recognition.
LGBT news outlet abroad (Jan 2016): the first openly LGBT member of this country's legislature took office - a milestone for LGBT political representation.

LGBT news outlet abroad (Jan 2018): this country and several regional peers were urged to abide by a regional human-rights court's landmark 2017 advisory opinion requiring marriage equality and gender recognition.
blindLocalsOnly: The femicide-law exclusion of trans women and the still-absent legal gender recognition are resident-facing; the 147-case / 29-murder toll falls on residents.
